doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How Dr. Tibbs's organ playing influenced her
summary: She did not study with Tibbs but was knocked out by his pipe organ playing.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Now, how did that overlap with your experience at the church, and in your study of gospel music, of Mr. Tibbs, is that correct, the choir director?
Oh, I didn‘t study with him, but I was really influenced. I heard him, Dr. Tibbs. He played the organ. He played the pipe organ and stuff, and he showed me things, you know.
How were you influenced, specifically, by him? Was it harmonically? I mean, when you think about it, how did he influence you?
He influenced me because he was bad. [laughs] I mean, he was bad. He played . . . you know, I listened to him. He just, he just knocked me down. You know, yeah, right.
